subject: chemistry-9
description: Authentic 12-mark Section A Federal Board examination simulator covering Nature of Science, Matter, and Atomic Structure by Lecturer Ayesha Amjad.

questions.question: The branch of chemistry concerned with the large-scale production of useful substances is:
questions.explanation: Industrial chemistry is the branch of chemistry that applies physical and chemical processes toward the transformation of raw materials into products that are of benefit to humanity.

questions.question: Which one of the following can be chemically broken down into simpler substances?
questions.explanation: Ammonia (NH3) is a chemical compound composed of nitrogen and hydrogen and can be decomposed into its elements, whereas oxygen, sulphur, and iron are elements.

questions.question: Why is the proton number unique to each element and used to arrange elements in the modern periodic table?

options.A: Protons determine the mass of the element
options.B: Protons define the atomic number of the element
options.C: Protons indicate the number of neutrons in the nucleus
options.D: Protons indicate the number of electrons in the atom

questions.explanation: Every chemical element has a characteristic, fixed number of protons in its nucleus, known as its atomic number (Z), which uniquely defines its chemical identity.

questions.question: Crystallization will spontaneously occur in which of the following solutions upon slight cooling or disturbance?
questions.explanation: A supersaturated solution holds more dissolved solute than a saturated solution at the given temperature; it is metastable and crystallizes readily.

questions.question: The total number of orbitals in the third energy level (M-shell, n = 3) is:
questions.explanation: The total number of orbitals in any principal quantum shell is given by n². For M shell (n = 3), n² = 3² = 9 orbitals (one 3s, three 3p, and five 3d orbitals).

questions.question: Which radioisotope of uranium is primarily used as fuel in commercial nuclear power plants?
questions.explanation: Uranium-235 (U-235) undergoes induced nuclear fission when struck by thermal neutrons, releasing tremendous thermal energy used in power reactors.

questions.question: In his pioneering gold foil experiment, Ernest Rutherford used which type of particles:
questions.explanation: Alpha particles are doubly ionized helium atoms (He²⁺) consisting of 2 protons and 2 neutrons, which are identical to helium nuclei.

questions.question: The rest mass of an electron in SI units is approximately:
questions.explanation: The rest mass of an electron is 9.10938 × 10⁻³¹ kg (or 9.11 × 10⁻²⁸ g).

questions.question: The statement “it is impossible to determine simultaneously both the position and momentum of an electron with absolute precision” is known as:
questions.explanation: Werner Heisenberg formulated the uncertainty principle in 1927: Δx · Δp ≥ h / (4π).

questions.question: The density of pure liquid water at standard laboratory temperature (4°C) is approximately:
questions.explanation: At 4°C water reaches its maximum density of 1.000 g/cm³, and around room temperature (25°C) its density is 0.997 g/cm³.

questions.question: The second principal shell (L shell, n = 2) consists of which subshells:
questions.explanation: For n = 2, the azimuthal quantum number l can have values 0 and 1, corresponding to the 2s and 2p subshells.

questions.question: A subshell that can accommodate a maximum of 6 electrons is designated as:
questions.explanation: The maximum electron capacity of a subshell is 2(2l + 1). For p subshell (l = 1), maximum capacity is 2(2·1 + 1) = 6 electrons.
